FR-R2: partly built: a tester's observation (through the cockpit, an embed or MCP) becomes a change card signed by the tester; triage classifies it as a defect, change request, new requirement, question, infrastructure change or incident, links it to the requirements the analyst names that the spec holds, and routes it: a defect straight back to build with a regression criterion, a requirement change or new need to a business decision first (kernel/change.py). Not built: the brief's classes 'UI gap' and 'data' do not exist (a UI gap is triaged as a change request and returns to stage 4, not stage 2); an observation is linked to no owner (the card names the tester and who may decide, not the requirement's owner); and the cockpit triages by rule with no model, so an observation filed there links to no requirement unless the tester names one in the text. It would take two more classes in CLASSES and WAY_BACK, an owner taken from the linked requirement's decided_by, and the analyst's triage behind the cockpit route.
FR-R3: partly built: at pilot and production a release waits on a validation card that only a business owner or product owner may decide, with the verdicts accept, fix, change and keep, and the holdout report and the staging address on it (kernel/deliver.py, kernel/canon.py). Not built: the card carries the holdout run only, not the testers' own report (their observations and the try-it checklist's evidence states are not attached to it); and a fix or change verdict only names the change loop in the release's handoff: nothing opens a change card from it, and kernel.change.triage on the validation card raises KeyError('text'). It would take attaching the release's try-it checklist and its end-user change cards to the card, and a step that turns a fix or change verdict into a change card carrying the person's reason.
FR-S2: built in part (kernel/epics.py): epics with owner, criterion, requirements and linked questions, person-signed, qualified, and the hierarchy to tasks, commits and tests. Not built: an agent drafting an epic into canon/inbox/ as its own card kind (an agent proposes one in the channel or through Ask Rihma's proposal instead), rejecting or freezing an epic with a reason, and the Watch's drift alert for orphan features and epics.
FR-S3: partly built: agents file only cards (an escalation, an update, a change, a concept; the cockpit assistant's actions are proposals a person confirms), a decision needs a named person, the Inbox's open cards empty as people decide, a merge needs a passing gate, and a Gnomon transcript is kept as evidence in the ledger only (kernel/canon.py, kernel/dispatch.py, kernel/assistant.py, adapters/gnomon_ingest.py). Not built: the exchange folder is never deleted once concluded: Canon.note writes notes to canon/exchange, and nothing marks a thread concluded or removes it. It would take a conclude step that deletes a thread's notes and keeps a ledger record of the conclusion.
FR-S5: not built: none of the nine narrow roles (scribe, concept, translator, status, watch, board keeper, onboarder, environment watch, deploy agent) exists as an agent with a one-page card that is both its instruction and its limit. Some of their work is kernel code with no agent (status lines in kernel/status.py, delivery in kernel/deliver.py, overdue assumptions in Canon.overdue), and the model roles that exist (analyst, holdout author, builder, verifier, assistant) get their limits compiled into Gnomon's roles.toml by kernel/lanes.py (tools, write scope, step caps, one description line), not from a card. It would take one card per role (instruction, tools, read and write scope, where it posts) compiled into a Gnomon role the way kernel/lanes.py compiles the builder and the verifier.
FR-T2: partly built: the customer-facing embed answers only from its title, its public brief and the conversation (kernel/embeds.py), and each persona's inbox holds only the cards it may decide, so IT is put environment and technical decisions only (CARD_DECIDERS in kernel/canon.py). Not built: the cockpit's and the MCP server's reads are not scoped by persona. The persona is whatever the person signed in on loopback picks, and the dashboard and the Floor (spend), the Cell (each run's priced cost) and the project view (health with its delivery forecast) answer every caller alike, IT and the customer's personas included; rihma_floor serves spend to any MCP persona. Nothing classifies data as internal or commercial. It would take a visibility class on each read model's fields, a persona filter applied server-side in the cockpit and the MCP server, and a sign-in that binds a person to the personas they hold.
FR-T3: partly built: the factory's reads reach a developer's own coding agent over MCP as views of the kernel's read models, and everything another tool sends in (a feed, chat or email signal, an MCP proposal, an embed, an adopted project's upstream sync) ends as an open card a person decides, never directly in the canon (kernel/signals.py, mcp/server.py, kernel/embeds.py, kernel/adopt.py). Not built: no board or digest is generated into Teams, Jira, Azure Boards or Planner (there is no connector; the cockpit and MCP are the only views), and the rule that an integration is built only after the agreement has worked by hand is a practice the code neither enforces nor records. It would take a digest renderer from the canon for each party and one outbound connector at a time, each opened only by a recorded decision that the manual agreement has worked.
